subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw expose an explicit persistent plain-text TUI mode, and what canonical ASCII replacements should it guarantee across OpenClaw and pi-tui-owned rendering?
rationale: The accessibility need and affected paths are clear, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config surface and the choice determines a durable user-facing contract across multiple renderers and an upstream dependency seam.

options.title: Add a coherent plain-text mode
options.body: Add a documented `ui.accessibility.plainText`-style preference and define one tested ASCII symbol set across all TUI render paths and pi-tui wrappers.

options.title: Use an explicit runtime control
options.body: Provide a TUI startup flag or in-product setting instead of permanent config, while preserving the same whole-surface ASCII contract.

options.title: Decline the mode
options.body: Keep current presentation and document terminal or screen-reader workarounds, accepting that the reported TUI accessibility friction remains.

recommendation.title: Add a coherent plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Add a documented `ui.accessibility.plainText`-style preference and define one tested ASCII symbol set across all TUI render paths and pi-tui wrappers.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history links this person most strongly to the original TUI/tool-display architecture and the cross-surface product contract at issue.
